study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Meijer et al., Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Toward Understanding Autism Heterogeneity: Identifying Clinical Subgroups and Neuroanatomical Deviations

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study combined data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) repositories I and II.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We combined the ABIDE repositories I (Di Martino et al., 2014) and II (Di Martino et al., 2017).

answer.ABIDE (I+II): Normative modeling training (90% of NAI) and testing (10% of NAI + autism group); clinical subgrouping via clustering of autistic participants.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Non-autistic individuals (NAI) were used to build the normative model (90% training, 10% testing). Autistic individuals were used as a clinical test set to identify individual neuroanatomical deviations and were clustered based on ADOS scores to identify clinical subgroups.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The dataset was split into a training set consisting of 90% of NAI and a test set consisting of all autistic individuals and the remaining 10% of NAI. ... we used clustering to identify distinct subgroups within autism... characterized the similarity (i.e., homogeneity) of normative modeling-derived neuroanatomical profiles.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Meijer2024.pdf.md: Method / Participants, Method / Normative Modeling

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A total of 744 male NAI were used for the normative modeling analysis. The training set comprised 90% of this sample (calculated as 744 * 0.9 = 669.6, rounded to 670).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: This resulted in a sample of 690 autistic and 744 NAI ... included in the normative modeling analysis ... The dataset was split into a training set consisting of 90% of NAI and a test set consisting of all autistic individuals and the remaining 10% of NAI.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Meijer2024.pdf.md: Method / Participants, Method / Normative Modeling

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are reported for the male NAI pool (N=886) from which the final normative modeling sample (N=744) was derived. The stats for the training subset (90%) are not explicitly reported, although the authors state that age was evenly distributed across sets.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: NAI (N = 886) ... M = 16.58, SD = 8.96, Range = 5.9 - 64 ... We also ensured that age, FIQ and site were evenly distributed across the training and test sets.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The primary analysis excluded females due to low sample size across sites, focusing on a male-only sample (N=744 NAI for modeling).
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: primary analyses were conducted in males only due to limited sample size of females (N autism = 130, N NAI = 280) ... This resulted in a sample of ... 744 NAI ... included in the normative modeling analysis.
